Step 4 Learn deep learning

Time: 2-3 months. Deep learning uses large neural networks. It is what makes image, sound and language AI work. PyTorch is the recommended framework.

LearnProjects to build
  • Neural networks
  • CNNs (convolutional neural networks, for images)
  • Transfer learning (reuse a model someone already trained)
  • Flower classification
  • Plant disease detection
  • Image recognition
Install with pip install torch torchvision. For the image projects, put photos in folders named after their class: flowers/train/rose/…, flowers/train/tulip/…, and so on. A GPU makes training much faster, but a CPU is enough for the small examples here.

net.py · your first neural network

A neural network is layers of numbers. Each Linear layer mixes its inputs, and ReLU between layers lets the network learn curves, not only straight lines. This one takes 4 numbers in and gives 3 scores out.

Read the full code

Practise it part by part

Imports

Import torch, then import nn from torch.

The layers

Write class Net(nn.Module):. In __init__ call super().__init__() and set self.layers to an nn.Sequential of nn.Linear(4, 16), nn.ReLU() and nn.Linear(16, 3), one per line.

The forward pass

Add forward(self, x) that returns self.layers(x).

Try it

Create net from Net() and print what it gives for one random row: net(torch.rand(1, 4)).

cnn.py · a convolutional network for images

A CNN slides small filters over an image to find edges, then shapes, then objects. Conv2d finds the patterns and MaxPool2d shrinks the picture. For a 224 by 224 colour image, two pools leave 56 by 56.

x.flatten(1) turns each picture from a stack of 2D maps into one long list, which the Linear layer needs.

Read the full code

Practise it part by part

The class and its filters

Import nn from torch. Write class SmallCNN(nn.Module): with __init__(self, classes). After super().__init__(), set self.features to an nn.Sequential of: nn.Conv2d(3, 16, 3, padding=1), nn.ReLU(), nn.MaxPool2d(2), nn.Conv2d(16, 32, 3, padding=1), nn.ReLU(), nn.MaxPool2d(2).

The final layer

Set self.classifier to nn.Linear(32 * 56 * 56, classes). It turns the flattened features into one score per class.

The forward pass

Write forward(self, x): set x to self.features(x), then return self.classifier(x.flatten(1)).

transfer.py · transfer learning for flowers

Training a CNN from nothing needs a lot of photos. Transfer learning starts from resnet18, which already learned to see on millions of images. You freeze it, replace only the last layer with your own classes, and train that layer. A few hundred photos are enough.

One training step: predict, measure the mistake (loss), work out how each weight caused it (backward), and nudge the weights (step). The loss should go down each epoch. For plant disease detection, use the same file with folders named after each disease and one for healthy leaves.

Read the full code

Practise it part by part

Imports

Import torch; nn from torch; datasets, models, transforms from torchvision; and DataLoader from torch.utils.data. One line each.

Load the photos

Make transform with transforms.Compose of transforms.Resize((224, 224)) and transforms.ToTensor(). Load "flowers/train" with datasets.ImageFolder into train_data, then make a DataLoader called loader with batch_size=16 and shuffle=True.

Reuse a trained model

Load models.resnet18(weights="DEFAULT") into model. Loop over model.parameters() and set param.requires_grad to False. Replace model.fc with nn.Linear(model.fc.in_features, len(train_data.classes)).

Loss and optimizer

Create loss_fn as nn.CrossEntropyLoss() and optimizer as torch.optim.Adam over model.fc.parameters() with lr=0.001.

The training loop

Loop epoch over range(3), and inside it loop images, labels over loader. For each batch: optimizer.zero_grad(), loss = loss_fn(model(images), labels), loss.backward(), optimizer.step(). After each epoch print "epoch", epoch + 1, "loss" and loss.item().

Save it

Save the learned weights with torch.save(model.state_dict(), "flowers.pt").

Step 5 Learn computer vision

Time: build it as you go. Computer vision is AI that works with images and video. It builds on Stage 4, and it is the area behind your football and farm ideas.

LearnProjects to build
  • OpenCV: read, change and measure images
  • YOLO: find and label objects in one pass
  • Segmentation: colour every pixel that belongs to an object
  • Object tracking: follow an object between frames
  • Video analytics: do all of this on every frame
  • Flower detection
  • Red/yellow card detection in football
  • Traffic sign recognition
  • Pest detection for agriculture
Install with pip install opencv-python ultralytics. Put a photo called pitch.jpg and a short video called match.mp4 in your project folder.

colour.py · OpenCV basics and a yellow-card finder

OpenCV reads an image as a grid of numbers. Colours are easier to pick out in the HSV space (hue, saturation, value) than in the normal BGR order, so you convert first and then keep only the pixels inside a colour range.

A big count of yellow pixels in one spot is a hint of a yellow card (or a yellow shirt, so a real project checks the shape and size too). For red, you need two ranges, because red sits at both ends of the hue scale. A hand-made colour filter is a good first step, and a trained YOLO model is the better final one.

Read the full code

Practise it part by part

Load the image

Import cv2 and read "pitch.jpg" into image with cv2.imread.

Find the edges

Make gray with cv2.cvtColor(image, cv2.COLOR_BGR2GRAY). Make blur with cv2.GaussianBlur(gray, (5, 5), 0). Make edges with cv2.Canny(blur, 50, 150). Save it with cv2.imwrite("edges.png", edges).

Find yellow

Convert image to hsv with cv2.COLOR_BGR2HSV. Make mask with cv2.inRange(hsv, (20, 100, 100), (35, 255, 255)). Print "yellow pixels:" and cv2.countNonZero(mask).

detect.py · object detection with YOLO

YOLO looks at a picture once and returns boxes, each with a class and a confidence. The small model yolov8n.pt downloads itself the first time. To detect your own things (flowers, pests, cards), train it on your own labelled photos. For segmentation, use yolov8n-seg.pt the same way.

Read the full code

Practise it part by part

Load the model

Import YOLO from ultralytics. Create model with YOLO("yolov8n.pt").

Run it

Call the model on "pitch.jpg" and keep the answer in results.

Read the boxes

Loop over results[0].boxes as box. Get the class name with model.names[int(box.cls)] into name, and print name and float(box.conf).

track.py · object tracking and video analytics

A video is just many pictures. Run detection on each frame, and give the tracker persist=True so an object keeps the same ID from frame to frame. That is how you count players, cars or pests that move.

Read the full code

Practise it part by part

Open the video

Import cv2 and YOLO from ultralytics. Create model from "yolov8n.pt", and open "match.mp4" into video with cv2.VideoCapture.

Read frames

Write while video.isOpened():. Inside, read ok, frame from video.read(), and break if not ok.

Track and show

Inside the loop, track the frame with model.track(frame, persist=True) into results. Show results[0].plot() in a window called "tracking" with cv2.imshow. Break if cv2.waitKey(1) == ord("q").

Clean up

After the loop, call video.release() and cv2.destroyAllWindows().

Step 6 Learn generative AI and LLMs

Time: build it as you go. This is the part of AI you already started with RAG and OpenRouter. The AI tab builds the full app. Here you learn the pieces one at a time.

LearnProjects to build
  • Transformers: the model design behind every modern LLM
  • Embeddings: text turned into numbers that capture meaning
  • Vector databases: store and search embeddings
  • RAG: find the right text first, then let the model answer from it
  • LangChain: glue for chains, prompts and tools
  • Ollama: run models on your own computer
  • vLLM: serve models fast on a GPU server
  • Agriculture chatbot
  • Document Q&A system
  • PDF assistant
  • Company knowledge-base chatbot
Install with pip install transformers torch sentence-transformers chromadb ollama. For the RAG file you also need Ollama running with llama3.2:3b pulled (see the AI tab, Step 2). The AI tab also covers LangChain, OpenRouter, vLLM, Claude and ChatGPT.

transformer.py · use a transformer model

A transformer reads all the words of a text together and learns which words matter to which. The pipeline helper from Hugging Face downloads a ready-made one in a single line.

The first run downloads the model. The answer is a label (POSITIVE or NEGATIVE) and a score between 0 and 1.

Read the full code

Practise it part by part

Load the model

Import pipeline from transformers. Create classifier with pipeline("sentiment-analysis").

Classify two sentences

Print the classifier's answer for "The harvest was excellent this year", then for "The pests destroyed most of the beans".

embed.py · embeddings and similarity

An embedding turns a sentence into a list of numbers so that sentences with similar meaning end up close together. Cosine similarity measures the closeness. This is how search by meaning works.

The first two sentences share no important word, yet their score is high, because they mean the same thing. The third scores low. A keyword search would miss the first pair.

Read the full code

Practise it part by part

Load the model and encode

Import SentenceTransformer and util from sentence_transformers. Create model with SentenceTransformer("all-MiniLM-L6-v2"). Make a list sentences of "Maize needs rain", "Corn grows in wet weather" and "The match ended 2-1". Encode it into vectors.

Compare them

Print util.cos_sim of vectors[0] and vectors[1], then of vectors[0] and vectors[2].

rag.py · a tiny RAG in one file

RAG (retrieval-augmented generation) has three steps. Store your documents in a vector database. When a question comes, retrieve the most similar text. Then augment the prompt with that text and let the model generate the answer from it, so it uses your facts and not its guesses.

Chroma turns the documents into embeddings for you, and the question too. That is why the maize sentence is found. Swap the two sentences for chunks of a PDF and you have a PDF assistant. Add a FastAPI route (Stage 1) and you have a chatbot your team can call.

Read the full code

Practise it part by part

Store the documents

Import chromadb and ollama. Create client with chromadb.Client() and a collection docs named "farm" with client.create_collection. Add two documents with docs.add: ids "1" and "2", and the two sentences about maize and tomato blight.

Retrieve

Set question to "When do I plant maize?". Search with docs.query(query_texts=[question], n_results=1) into found, and take the text as context from found["documents"][0][0].

Augment and generate

Build prompt as an f-string: Answer using only this text:, a newline, the context, a blank line, then Question: and the question. Call ollama.chat with model="llama3.2:3b" and one user message holding the prompt. Print the reply text.

Step 7 Learn MLOps (advanced)

Time: after the stages above. MLOps is the engineering that gets a model out of your notebook and keeps it working in production. This is what companies need when deploying AI systems.

LearnProjects to build
  • Docker: package the app and its libraries
  • Git: version your code (see the Git tab)
  • GitHub Actions: run tests and builds automatically
  • MLflow: record experiments and models
  • Kubernetes: run many copies at scale (later)
  • Put your FastAPI model in a Docker image
  • Run tests on every push with GitHub Actions
  • Track three training runs in MLflow

Dockerfile · package your API

A Dockerfile is the recipe for an image: a sealed box with Python, your libraries and your code, which runs the same on your laptop and on a server. This one packages the FastAPI main.py from Stage 1.

Copying requirements.txt first means Docker re-uses the slow install step until your requirements change. --host 0.0.0.0 lets traffic reach the app from outside the container. Add a .dockerignore file with .venv and .env so they never go into the image.

Read the full code

Practise it part by part

Base image and packages

Start FROM python:3.12-slim. Set WORKDIR /app. Copy requirements.txt to . with COPY and install it with RUN pip install --no-cache-dir -r requirements.txt.

Your code and start command

Copy everything with COPY . ., EXPOSE 8000, and set CMD to the list ["uvicorn", "main:app", "--host", "0.0.0.0", "--port", "8000"].

Build and run the image

Run these in the folder that holds the Dockerfile. Docker Desktop (or Docker Engine) must be installed and running.

Open http://127.0.0.1:8000/crops/maize to see the same answer as before, now from inside the container. Stop it with Ctrl+C.

Read the full code

Practise it part by part

Build it

Build an image tagged crop-api from the current folder with docker build -t.

Run it and look

Run it with port 8000 on your computer mapped to port 8000 in the container using -p 8000:8000. Then, in another terminal, list running containers with docker ps.

GitHub Actions · run tests on every push

A workflow is a file in .github/workflows/. GitHub reads it and runs the steps on a fresh machine every time you push. Add a test file first (for example test_main.py) so pytest has something to run.

YAML uses spaces for structure, never tabs, so keep the indent exact. After you push, open the Actions tab of your repository to see a green tick or a red cross. Push the file with Git as shown in the Git tab.

Read the full code

Practise it part by part

When and where

Set the name to tests, run on: [push], and define jobs with one job test that runs-on: ubuntu-latest.

The steps

Under steps: add, one per line or block: uses: actions/checkout@v4; uses: actions/setup-python@v5 with python-version: "3.12"; run: pip install -r requirements.txt pytest httpx; and run: pytest. Each step starts with a dash.

track_run.py · record experiments with MLflow

After a few experiments you forget which settings gave which score. MLflow writes down the settings (parameters), the scores (metrics) and the model of every run, so you can compare them later.

Install with pip install mlflow. After running the file, start the web page with mlflow ui and open http://127.0.0.1:5000 to compare the three runs. Kubernetes comes later: it runs many Docker containers across many machines and restarts them when they fail. Learn Docker well first.

Read the full code

Practise it part by part

Imports and data

Import mlflow, load_iris from sklearn.datasets, RandomForestClassifier from sklearn.ensemble and train_test_split from sklearn.model_selection. Then load and split the data exactly as in classify.py.

One run per setting

Loop trees over [10, 50, 100]. Inside, open with mlflow.start_run(): and train a RandomForestClassifier(n_estimators=trees, random_state=42) on the training data.

Log it

Still inside the run, log the parameter "trees" with mlflow.log_param and the metric "accuracy" with mlflow.log_metric, using model.score(X_test, y_test).

Step 8 Check that it worked

  • Python: run python calculator.py and type 6 * 7. It prints 42.0. Start the API with uvicorn main:app --reload and open /crops/maize.
  • Data: python analyze.py prints the table and creates harvest.png.
  • Machine learning: houses.py prints a train score and a test score. If the train score is much higher, you are overfitting.
  • Deep learning: transfer.py prints a loss for each epoch, and the loss goes down. A file flowers.pt appears.
  • Computer vision: detect.py prints object names with confidence scores, and track.py shows boxes with ID numbers on the video.
  • Generative AI: rag.py answers that maize is planted at the start of the long rains.
  • MLOps: docker run -p 8000:8000 crop-api serves the API, the Actions tab shows a green tick, and mlflow ui lists three runs.

If something fails

What you seeWhyFix
ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'pandas'The package is not installed, or the virtual environment is not active.Activate .venv (the prompt shows (.venv)), then pip install pandas.
FileNotFoundError: crops.csvPython looks in the folder where you ran it, not where the script is.cd to the project folder first, or check the file name.
KeyError: 'yield'The column name in the CSV differs from the one in your code (spelling, capitals, spaces).Print df.columns and use exactly what it shows.
ValueError: Found input variables with inconsistent numbers of samplesX and y have different numbers of rows.Check both with .shape and drop rows with missing values using df.dropna().
Test score far lower than train scoreOverfitting, or too little data.Use a simpler model, add more data, and never tune on the test set.
RuntimeError: mat1 and mat2 shapes cannot be multipliedThe size of one layer does not match the size of the one before it.Print x.shape before the failing layer and fix the number in nn.Linear.
cv2.imread gives None / error in cvtColorThe image path is wrong, so no picture was loaded.Check the file name and the folder you run from.
ConnectionError when calling OllamaOllama is not running, or the model is not pulled.Start Ollama and run ollama pull llama3.2:3b.
Docker: cannot connect to the Docker daemonDocker Desktop or the Docker service is not running.Start it and try again.
GitHub Actions: workflow does not runThe file is not in .github/workflows/ on the default branch, or the YAML indent is wrong.Move the file, fix the indent, and push again.
Your AI roadmap

Python, data, ML, deep learning, vision, LLMs, MLOps

You now have a map and a first piece of working code for every stage. The next step is a real project for each stage, using your own football and crop data. Finish small projects, put them on GitHub (see the Git tab), and move to the next stage only when the last one feels easy.

Interview questions

Try to answer each one aloud before you open it.

Why learn Python and data analysis before machine learning?

Models are trained on data, and most of the work is loading, cleaning and understanding it. Without Python and Pandas you cannot prepare the data, and without the chart habit you cannot tell when the data or the result is wrong.

What is the difference between classification, regression and clustering?

Classification predicts a label (win, draw or loss). Regression predicts a number (a price or a yield). Clustering finds groups in data that has no labels.

Why do you split data into training and test sets?

To measure how the model does on data it has never seen. A model scored on its own training data looks better than it really is.

What is overfitting and how do you fight it?

The model memorises the training data and fails on new data. You see a high train score and a low test score. Use more data, a simpler model, regularisation or early stopping, and check on a separate test set.

Why is accuracy not always a good metric?

With rare classes, a model that always predicts the common class gets a high accuracy and is useless. Precision, recall and the confusion matrix show what really happens.

What is transfer learning and why use it?

You start from a model already trained on a huge dataset, freeze most of it, and train only a new last layer on your data. It needs far fewer photos, less time and less hardware.

What does a CNN do that a plain neural network does not?

Its filters slide over the image and look at small neighbourhoods, so it finds the same pattern (an edge or a petal) wherever it appears, with far fewer weights than connecting every pixel to every neuron.

What is the difference between image classification and object detection?

Classification gives one label for the whole picture. Detection finds each object, draws a box around it and labels it. Segmentation goes further and marks which pixels belong to each object.

What is an embedding?

A list of numbers that represents the meaning of a text (or image), so that things with similar meaning are close together. It is the basis of search by meaning and of RAG.

What problem does RAG solve?

An LLM only knows its training data and may invent answers. RAG first retrieves the relevant text from your own documents and puts it in the prompt, so the answer is based on your facts and can point to its source.

Ollama or vLLM, which one and when?

Ollama is the easy way to run a model on your own computer, good for learning and small tools. vLLM is built to serve many users quickly on a GPU server, so it fits production.

Why use Docker for a model API?

The image holds the exact Python version and libraries, so the app runs the same on your laptop, a colleague's computer and the server. It also makes deployment and scaling repeatable.

What does MLflow track, and why does it matter?

Parameters, metrics and models for each run. It lets you compare experiments, reproduce the best one, and know exactly which model went to production.

Put your project on GitHub from the command line. You will install Git, tell it who you are, log in to your GitHub account, turn your project folder into a repository, make a commit, and push it. Then you will learn the daily routine, branches, pull requests, and how to fix the usual mistakes. The examples use the rag-app folder from the other tabs, but the steps work for any project.

Use any terminal: Command Prompt (cmd), PowerShell, Terminal on macOS, or a Linux shell. The Git commands are the same everywhere. Where Windows differs, the text says so. Replace YOUR-USERNAME, Your Name and you@example.com with your own details.

Never type a password, token or key into this page. The boxes below save your text in your browser. Practise with the placeholders shown, and type real secrets only in your own terminal.

Step 1 Understand Git and GitHub

Git is a program on your computer. It records snapshots of your project, called commits, so you can see what changed and go back.
GitHub is a website that stores a copy of your repository online, so you can back it up, share it, and work with others. Git is the tool, GitHub is the place you send the snapshots.
Remote: the online copy. By convention it is named origin.

Your files
↓ git add
Staging area (what goes into the next snapshot)
↓ git commit
Local repository (your history)
↓ git push
GitHub (origin)

Step 2 Install Git and say who you are

Install Git from git-scm.com. On Windows, accept the defaults, which also install Git Credential Manager, the helper that remembers your GitHub login. On macOS, run xcode-select --install or use Homebrew. On Ubuntu or Debian, run sudo apt install git. Close and reopen your terminal afterwards.

Check that Git is installed

This prints the version number. If your terminal says the command is not found, Git is not installed yet, or you need to open a new terminal.

Read the commands

Practise them

Check the version

Write the command that prints the Git version.

Set your name and email

Every commit records who made it. --global saves the setting for every project on this computer, so you do this once. Use the same email as your GitHub account, or the private "noreply" address GitHub shows in Settings, Emails. init.defaultBranch main makes new repositories start on a branch called main, which matches what GitHub uses. The last line prints your settings so you can check them.

Read the commands

Practise them

Set name and email

Write two git config --global commands, one per line: user.name set to "Your Name", then user.email set to "you@example.com".

Choose main and check

Add git config --global init.defaultBranch main, then git config --global --list on the next line.

Step 3 Log in to your GitHub account

Create an account at github.com if you don't have one. GitHub no longer accepts your account password for git push. You log in in one of three ways. Option A, the GitHub CLI, is the easiest, so start there.

OptionHow it worksBest for
A. GitHub CLI (gh)You run gh auth login, approve in your browser, and Git is set up to use that login.Most people. Works on every system.
B. Personal access tokenYou create a token on GitHub and paste it when Git asks for a password.When you can't install gh.
C. SSH keyYou make a key pair and give GitHub the public half. No password prompts after that.People who push every day.

Option A: the GitHub CLI

Log in with gh

Install the GitHub CLI from cli.github.com (on Windows you can also run winget install --id GitHub.cli), then open a new terminal. gh auth login asks a few questions. Choose GitHub.com, then HTTPS, answer Yes to "Authenticate Git with your GitHub credentials?", and choose Login with a web browser. It shows a one-time code. Press Enter, paste the code on the page that opens, and sign in. gh auth status then confirms who you are logged in as.

Read the commands

Practise them

Log in and check

Write gh auth login, then gh auth status on the next line.

Option B: a personal access token

On GitHub, open your profile picture, then Settings, Developer settings, Personal access tokens, and create a token. A fine-grained token limited to one repository is safest, with read and write access to Contents. A classic token with the repo scope also works. Copy it straight away, because GitHub shows it only once.

The first time you run git push over HTTPS, Git asks for a Username, which is your GitHub username, and a Password, where you paste the token, not your account password. Nothing shows as you paste, which is normal. On Windows, Git Credential Manager remembers it, and it may open a browser sign-in instead, which is also fine. Treat a token like a password: never put it in code, in .env files you commit, or in a chat.

Option C: an SSH key

Make an SSH key and test it

ssh-keygen makes a key pair. Press Enter to accept the default file, and choose a passphrase if you like. The public key is the file ending in .pub. Print it, copy it, and add it on GitHub under Settings, SSH and GPG keys, New SSH key. Never share the file without .pub. The last line checks that GitHub recognises you. On Windows cmd, print the key with type %USERPROFILE%\.ssh\id_ed25519.pub instead of cat.

With SSH, your remote address looks like git@github.com:YOUR-USERNAME/rag-app.git and not https://github.com/.... Use one style consistently.

Read the commands

Practise them

Make and test the key

Write ssh-keygen with -t ed25519 and -C "you@example.com". Then print ~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub with cat. Then test with ssh -T git@github.com.

Step 4 Turn your project into a repository

Open your terminal in the project folder. On Windows cmd, change drive and folder in one go with cd /d D:\projects\rag-app (the /d lets cd switch drives). First, tell Git what to leave out.

.gitignore

Create a file named exactly .gitignore in the project folder, before your first commit. Each line is a name or folder Git must never track.

The first line matters most. .env holds your API keys. A key pushed to GitHub can be found and used by anyone, even in a private repository's history if it is ever made public. The other lines skip the virtual environment, the vector databases, Python's cache and the Angular packages, which are large and can be rebuilt.

Read the file

Practise it

Ignore secrets and rebuildable folders

Write nine lines: .env, .venv/, chroma_db/, chroma_db_openrouter/, chroma_db_vllm/, chroma_db_claude/, chroma_db_openai/, __pycache__/ and node_modules/.

Angular makes its own repository. ng new frontend runs git init inside frontend, so Git later treats that folder as a separate repository and skips its files. Before your first git add, delete that hidden folder: rmdir /s /q frontend\.git on Windows cmd, or rm -rf frontend/.git on macOS and Linux. Next time, use ng new frontend --skip-git.

Create the repository

git init creates a hidden .git folder, where Git keeps the history. git status shows what Git sees. Your files appear as "untracked", and .env and .venv should not be listed, because .gitignore hides them.

Read the commands

Practise them

Go to the folder and start

Write cd rag-app, then git init, then git status, one per line.

Make your first commit

git add . puts every change into the staging area, the list of what the next snapshot contains. git commit -m saves the snapshot with a short message that says what changed. git branch -M main renames the current branch to main, which is harmless if it is already called that.

Run git status between add and commit, and read the green list. If you see .env there, stop: your .gitignore is wrong or misnamed.

Read the commands

Practise them

Stage and check

Write git add ., then git status.

Commit and name the branch

Write git commit -m with the message "First commit: RAG app". Then git branch -M main on the next line.

You need an empty repository on GitHub to push to. Make it in the browser: click +, then New repository, give it the name rag-app, choose Private if you want, and leave Add a README, .gitignore and license all unticked, so the repository starts empty. Or make it from the terminal with the CLI:

Create the repository with gh (optional)

Use this instead of the website if you logged in with gh. --private keeps it visible only to you, --source=. says the code is in the current folder, and --remote=origin connects it under the name origin. If you use this, the next step's git remote add line is already done, so skip it.

Read the commands

Practise them

Create it

Write gh repo create rag-app with --private, --source=. and --remote=origin.

Connect the remote and push

git remote add origin URL tells Git where the online copy lives. git remote -v lists your remotes so you can check the address. git push -u origin main uploads the main branch, and -u remembers the link, so later you only type git push. If you chose Option B, this is where Git asks for your username and token.

Refresh the repository page on GitHub. Your files should be there, and .env should not be.

Read the commands

Practise them

Add the remote

Push

The whole first push in six commands

This is everything from Step 4 and Step 5 in one list, which you will repeat for every new project. Run it from the project folder, after you create the empty repository on GitHub.

Read the commands

Initialise and commit

Name the branch, connect and push

Step 6 The daily routine

After the first push, each working session is the same loop: get the latest, change files, review, save a snapshot, and send it.

Pull, change, commit, push

git pull downloads new commits from GitHub, which matters when you work on two computers or with others. After you edit files, git status lists what changed and git diff shows the exact lines. Then you stage, commit with a message that says why, and push.

Read the commands

Practise them

Start and review

Write git pull, git status, then git diff, one per line.

Save and send

Write git add ., then git commit -m "Describe what you changed", then git push.

Look at the history

git log --oneline lists commits, newest first, one line each, with a short id. git show displays the latest commit and what it changed. Press q to leave a long list.

Read the commands

Practise them

Read the history

Write git log --oneline, then git show on the next line.

Step 7 Branches and pull requests

A branch is a separate line of work, so you can try something without touching main. A pull request (PR) asks GitHub to merge your branch into main, and it is where people review the change.

Work on a branch and open a pull request

git switch -c NAME creates a branch and moves onto it. The first push of a new branch needs -u origin NAME. gh pr create --fill opens a pull request using your commit message as the title. You can also click the green button GitHub shows after the push.

Read the commands

Practise them

Create the branch and commit

Write git switch -c add-feature, then git add ., then git commit -m "Add feature".

Push and open the PR

Write git push -u origin add-feature, then gh pr create --fill.

After the pull request is merged

Merge the pull request on GitHub with the Merge pull request button. Then bring your computer up to date and delete the finished branch. git switch main moves back to main, git pull downloads the merged work, and git branch -d removes the local branch.

Read the commands

Practise them

Tidy up

Write git switch main, git pull, then git branch -d add-feature, one per line.

Step 8 Get your project on another computer

Clone and rebuild

git clone downloads the repository, with its whole history, into a new folder. Because .gitignore kept some things out, you must rebuild them: make the virtual environment and install the packages (activate it first, with source .venv/bin/activate or .venv\Scripts\activate on Windows). Then create your .env file again by hand with your keys, because it was never uploaded, and run python ingest.py to rebuild the database.

Read the commands

Practise them

Clone and enter

Write git clone with https://github.com/YOUR-USERNAME/rag-app.git, then cd rag-app.

Rebuild the environment

Write python -m venv .venv, then pip install -r requirements.txt.

Step 9 Fix common mistakes

Stop tracking a file you already committed

Adding a file to .gitignore does not remove it from a repository that already tracks it. git rm --cached removes it from Git but keeps the file on your disk. Use it for .env, or for a folder with -r, such as git rm -r --cached chroma_db.

If a real key was ever pushed, deleting the file is not enough. The old commit still contains it. Treat the key as stolen: delete it in the provider's console, create a new one, and put the new one only in your local .env.

Read the commands

Practise them

Untrack and push

Write git rm --cached .env, then git commit -m "Stop tracking .env", then git push.

Undo cheat sheet

I want toCommandCareful
Throw away my edits to one filegit restore FILEThe edits are gone for good.
Take a file out of staginggit restore --staged FILESafe. The file keeps your edits.
Change the last commit messagegit commit --amend -m "New message"Only before you push it.
Undo a pushed commit safelygit revert HASHAdds a new commit that cancels the old one.
See which commit is whichgit log --onelineThe short id at the start of each line is the HASH.
Avoid git reset --hard and git push --force until you understand them. They can delete work, and a force push can erase other people's commits.

Step 10 Check that it worked

  • Run git --version and git config --global --list. You should see a version and your name and email.
  • Run gh auth status (or push once over HTTPS). It should show that you are logged in to github.com.
  • Run git status before your first commit. .env must not be listed.
  • After git push -u origin main, open https://github.com/YOUR-USERNAME/rag-app in your browser. Your files are there, and .env is not.
  • Change one line, then run git add ., git commit -m "test" and git push. The new commit shows on GitHub.

fatal: not a git repositoryYou are in a folder that has no .git, or in the wrong folder.Use cd to reach the project folder, or run git init there.
src refspec main does not match anyThere is no commit yet, or the branch has another name.Make a commit, then run git branch -M main and push again.
fatal: remote origin already existsYou already added a remote. gh repo create --remote=origin does this for you.Check it with git remote -v, or change it with git remote set-url origin NEWURL.
Authentication failed / Support for password authentication was removedGitHub does not accept your account password.Log in with gh auth login, or paste a personal access token as the password.
Permission denied (publickey)You use an SSH address, but GitHub doesn't have your public key.Add the .pub key on GitHub, or switch to HTTPS with git remote set-url origin https://github.com/YOUR-USERNAME/rag-app.git.
Repository not foundThe address is misspelled, or you are logged in as an account without access to that repository.Check git remote -v against the page address, and check gh auth status.
rejected: Updates were rejected because the remote contains work that you do not haveGitHub has commits you don't, such as a README you let it create.Run git pull --rebase origin main, then git push again.
warning: adding embedded git repository: frontendng new made its own .git inside frontend.Delete frontend/.git as in Step 4, then run git rm --cached frontend and git add . again.
File exceeds GitHub's 100 MB limit, or the push is hugenode_modules or a chroma_db folder was committed.Add it to .gitignore, run git rm -r --cached FOLDER, and commit again. If it is already pushed, use a new repository or clean the history.
.gitignore doesn't ignore a fileGit already tracks that file.Run git rm --cached FILE and commit.
Your project is on GitHub

Install, log in, commit, push

You can now put any folder under version control, connect it to your GitHub account from the command line, and keep it in sync. Good next steps are writing a README.md, protecting the main branch so changes go through pull requests, and adding a GitHub Actions workflow that tests your code on every push.

Interview questions

Try to answer each one aloud before you open it.

What is the difference between Git and GitHub?

Git is the version-control program that runs on your computer and records history. GitHub is a website that hosts copies of Git repositories and adds sharing, pull requests and issues. You can use Git without GitHub.

What do git add, git commit and git push each do?

git add puts changes in the staging area. git commit saves a snapshot of the staged changes in your local history. git push uploads your local commits to the remote repository.

What is origin?

The default name for the remote repository you cloned from or connected with git remote add. It is only a nickname for the address, and you can have several remotes.

What does -u do in git push -u origin main?

It sets the upstream: it links your local main to origin/main, so later git push and git pull know where to go without extra arguments.

Why must .env never be committed?

It holds secrets. Once a commit is pushed, anyone with access can read it, and Git history keeps old versions even after you delete the file. Ignore it with .gitignore, and rotate any key that leaked.

Why does GitHub ask for a token and not my password?

Passwords are weak for command-line use. A token can be limited to certain actions or one repository, can expire, and can be revoked without changing your account password.

HTTPS or SSH, which should I use?

HTTPS works through almost any network and is easy with gh auth login or a token. SSH uses a key pair and never asks for a password after setup. Both reach the same repository.

What is the difference between git pull and git fetch?

git fetch downloads new commits but leaves your files alone. git pull fetches and then merges them into your current branch.

What is a branch, and why open a pull request?

A branch is an independent line of commits, so you can work without disturbing main. A pull request proposes merging it, and gives teammates a place to review and discuss the change first.

What does git clone do that git init does not?

git clone copies an existing repository, with its full history and a remote already set. git init starts a brand-new empty repository with no history and no remote.

PSRS practical: a job recruitment system. You will build a FastAPI back end with MySQL, then a small Angular page. Part 1 is authentication and authorization (registration, login, password reset, roles, sessions, API keys). Part 2 is the recruitment logic (jobs, applications, scoring). Each part is its own module, so you can test it alone before joining them.

Angular page
↓ HTTP + Bearer token
FastAPI: auth.py (Part 1) and recruitment.py (Part 2)
↓ SQLAlchemy
MySQL: users, sessions, password_resets, api_keys, jobs, applications
Never type a real password or key into this page. The boxes save your text in your browser. Use the demo values shown here, and keep real secrets in your own files.

Step 1 Set up the project and the database

On Windows, activate the environment with venv\Scripts\activate. On macOS or Linux, use source venv/bin/activate. Do this each time you open a new terminal.

terminal

Create the folder, install the packages, and create the MySQL database and user.

pymysql talks to MySQL. cryptography is needed for MySQL 8 logins. bcrypt hashes passwords.

Read the full code

Practise it part by part

Make the project

Write three commands, one per line: make the folder psrs-api, go into it with cd, then create a virtual environment called venv with python -m venv.

Install packages

Write one pip install line for: fastapi uvicorn sqlalchemy pymysql cryptography bcrypt and "pydantic[email]" (in quotes).

Create the database

Run mysql -u root -p -e with one quoted SQL string that creates the database psrs, creates the user psrs@localhost identified by psrs_pass, and grants it all on psrs.*.

Step 2 Database connection and tables

db.py

One place that opens the MySQL connection. Every route asks for a session through get_db.

Read the full code

Practise it part by part

Engine and session factory

Import create_engine from sqlalchemy, and sessionmaker and DeclarativeBase from sqlalchemy.orm. Create engine for mysql+pymysql://psrs:psrs_pass@localhost/psrs with pool_pre_ping=True, then SessionLocal with sessionmaker(bind=engine, autoflush=False).

Base class

Write class Base(DeclarativeBase): with pass inside.

get_db

Write get_db(): open db = SessionLocal(), yield db inside try, and db.close() in finally.

models.py

Six tables. Tokens and API keys are stored only as SHA-256 hashes, never as the raw value. The unique pair job_id + email stops a candidate applying twice.

Read the full code

Practise it part by part

Imports

Import datetime from datetime; Boolean, DateTime, ForeignKey, String, Text, UniqueConstraint from sqlalchemy; Mapped, mapped_column from sqlalchemy.orm; and Base from db.

User

Write class User(Base) with __tablename__ = "users", an id primary key, a unique email (String 120), password_hash (String 100) and role (String 20, default "viewer").

Sessions and reset tokens

Write AuthSession (table sessions) and ResetToken (table password_resets). Each has id, a unique token_hash (String 64), user_id (ForeignKey users.id) and expires_at (DateTime). ResetToken also has used, a Boolean defaulting to False.

ApiKey

Write ApiKey (table api_keys) with id, name (String 60), a unique key_hash (String 64) and active (Boolean, default True).

Job

Write Job (table jobs) with id, title (String 120), department (String 80), location (String 80), salary (Mapped[int]) and active (Boolean, default True).

Application

Write Application (table applications) with id, name, email (String 120), job_id (ForeignKey jobs.id), resume (Text), and the integers resume_score, location_points, final_score. Add __table_args__ = (UniqueConstraint("job_id", "email"),).

Step 3 Part 1: authentication and authorization

security.py

The shared helpers: bcrypt hashing, session tokens, the "who is logged in" check, role checks (RBAC) and API key checks. A session token is random, only its hash is saved, and it expires after 2 hours.

Read the full code

Practise it part by part

Imports

Import hashlib and secrets; datetime, timedelta from datetime; bcrypt; Depends, Header, HTTPException from fastapi; Session from sqlalchemy.orm; get_db from db; and ApiKey, AuthSession, User from models.

Password and hash helpers

Write hash_password(password) using bcrypt.hashpw(password.encode(), bcrypt.gensalt()).decode(), verify_password(password, hashed) using bcrypt.checkpw, and sha(value) returning hashlib.sha256(value.encode()).hexdigest().

Create a session

Write create_session(db, user): make token = secrets.token_urlsafe(32), add an AuthSession with token_hash=sha(token), user_id=user.id and expires_at two hours from datetime.utcnow(), commit, and return the raw token.

Current user

Write current_user(authorization: str = Header(default=""), db: Session = Depends(get_db)). Remove Bearer with removeprefix, find the session by sha(token), and raise HTTPException(401, "Invalid or expired session") if it is missing or expires_at is in the past. Return db.get(User, row.user_id).

Role check (RBAC)

Write require_roles(*roles) that returns an inner function check(user: User = Depends(current_user)). If user.role is not in roles, raise HTTPException(403, "Not allowed for your role"). Otherwise return the user. Return check.

API key check

Write api_key_auth(x_api_key: str = Header(default=""), db: Session = Depends(get_db)). Look up an active ApiKey whose key_hash is sha(x_api_key). If none, raise HTTPException(401, "Invalid API key"). Otherwise return it.

auth.py

The auth routes: register, login, logout, password reset and API key creation. Failed logins are logged. The reset token is printed to the log so you can test; a real system would email it.

Read the full code

Practise it part by part

Imports and schemas

Import logging, secrets, datetime, timedelta; APIRouter, Depends, Header, HTTPException; BaseModel, EmailStr, Field from pydantic; Session; get_db; the models ApiKey, AuthSession, ResetToken, User; and from security the helpers create_session, current_user, hash_password, require_roles, sha, verify_password. Then make log = logging.getLogger("auth"), router = APIRouter(prefix="/auth", tags=["auth"]), and the schemas Register, Login, Forgot, Reset.

Register

Write POST /register (status 201). If the email already exists, raise HTTPException(409, "Email already registered"). Otherwise save a User with hash_password(body.password), log it, and return the id, email and role.

Login and logout

Write POST /login: if the user is missing or verify_password fails, log a warning and raise HTTPException(401, "Wrong email or password"); otherwise return {"token": create_session(db, user), "role": user.role}. Then POST /logout (needs current_user) that deletes the session with the token from the Authorization header.

Password reset

Write POST /forgot-password: if the user exists, save a ResetToken (hash of a new secrets.token_urlsafe(32), valid 15 minutes) and log the raw token. Always return the same message. Then POST /reset-password: find an unused token, reject it if missing or expired, set the new hashed password, mark it used, delete that user's sessions, commit.

API keys

Write POST /api-keys (status 201, admin only with require_roles("admin")) taking name. Make a raw key with secrets.token_urlsafe(32), save only sha(raw), log who made it, and return the raw key once with a note.

Step 4 Part 2: the recruitment logic

scoring.py

Pure functions with no database, so you can test them alone. The points come from the job location, not the candidate.

Read the full code

Practise it part by part

Location points

Write location_points(location): make place = location.strip().upper(). Return 3 for "REMOTE", 2 for "DAR ES SALAAM" or "DAR", and 1 for anything else.

Resume and final score

Write resume_score() returning random.randint(1, 10), and final_score(resume, location) returning their sum.

recruitment.py

Jobs and applications. Only admin and editor can add jobs. Anyone can see active jobs. A logged-in user can apply once per job. Third parties read jobs with an API key.

Read the full code

Practise it part by part

Imports and schemas

Import APIRouter, Depends, HTTPException; BaseModel, EmailStr, Field; Session; get_db; Application, Job, User; final_score, location_points, resume_score from scoring; and api_key_auth, current_user, require_roles from security. Make router = APIRouter(tags=["recruitment"]), the schemas JobIn (title, department, location, salary > 0) and ApplyIn (name, email, job_id, resume), and a helper job_dict(job).

Add and list jobs

Write POST /jobs (status 201, roles admin and editor) that saves Job(**body.model_dump()) and returns its id. Then GET /jobs that returns job_dict for every active job.

Apply

Write POST /applications (status 201, needs current_user). Return 404 if the job is missing or inactive, and 409 "You already applied for this job" if this email already applied. Score it with resume_score(), location_points(job.location) and final_score, save the Application, and return the summary with the message "Application processed successfully.".

Summary and API key route

Write GET /applications/summary (roles admin and editor) that joins Application with Job, sorts by final_score descending, and returns name, position, resume score, location priority and final score. Then GET /external/jobs protected by Depends(api_key_auth) that returns the active jobs.

main.py

The entry point. It creates the tables, allows the Angular page (port 4200) to call the API, and plugs in both routers.

Practise it part by part

App, CORS and routers

Create app = FastAPI(title="PSRS Recruitment"). Add CORSMiddleware allowing origin http://localhost:4200 with all methods and headers. Include auth.router and recruitment.router.

Needs Node.js and the Angular CLI (npm install -g @angular/cli). The page shows jobs, logs in, and lets a candidate apply.

Step 7 Check that it worked

  • Start uvicorn main:app --reload. The terminal should show no errors, and http://localhost:8000/docs should open. In MySQL, USE psrs; SHOW TABLES; lists six tables.
  • Register with POST /auth/register, then in MySQL run UPDATE psrs.users SET role='admin' WHERE email='you@example.com'; to make your first admin. Log in with POST /auth/login and copy the token.
  • Use curl or the Angular page and send Authorization: Bearer <token>. A viewer calling POST /jobs must get 403. An admin gets 201.
  • Add "Software Engineer" in Remote and "HR Officer" in DAR ES SALAAM. GET /jobs lists both. Apply to the first one: the location priority is 3 and the final score equals resume score + 3.
  • Apply to the same job with the same email again. You must get 409.
  • Call POST /auth/logout, then reuse the old token. You must get 401. Call /auth/forgot-password, copy the token from the log, and set a new password with /auth/reset-password.
  • Create a key with POST /auth/api-keys?name=partner as admin, then call GET /external/jobs with the header X-API-Key. Without the header you get 401.

Not included yet

Login, registration and reset pages in Angular (only login is on the jobs page), a "deactivate job" route, rate limiting on login, and automated tests. These are good next steps.

MySQL 8: the ten common DBA interview tasks, from creating tables to reading an execution plan. Each file starts with USE company_db; where needed, so you can run it on its own. Do the steps in order, because later ones use the tables from Step 1.

Practise on a test server only. These commands create and delete things. Never run them on a live database, and never type a real password into this page.

Start here Install MySQL and log in

A database has two parts. The server is the program that stores the data and runs in the background. The client is the tool you type in (a command-line program or a window like Workbench). So you install the server and a client, start the server, and then log in with the client.

1. What to install

SoftwareWhere fromWhat it is for
MySQL Community Server 8.xdev.mysql.com/downloads (on Windows use the MySQL Installer)The server. During setup you choose the password for the root user. Write it down.
MySQL WorkbenchSame site, or inside the MySQL InstallerA window for writing queries and managing users. Optional but friendly.
XAMPP (alternative)apachefriends.orgBundles MariaDB, which uses almost the same commands. Fine for learning, but the interview tasks assume MySQL.

terminal

After the installer finishes, close and reopen your terminal. Then check that the client is found. If your terminal says "not recognized", the program's bin folder is not on your PATH (see the table at the end of this part).

Read the full code

Practise it part by part

Check the client

Write mysql --version.

2. Start the server

terminal

The server must be running before you can log in.

Run the net start commands in Command Prompt opened as Administrator. Service names can differ, so open services.msc to see the exact name on your computer. On Linux use sudo systemctl start mysql. On macOS with Homebrew use brew services start mysql.

Practise it part by part

Write net start MySQL80.

This is the command-line login. You type your password when asked. It stays hidden while you type.

On a fresh Ubuntu server, sudo mysql may log you in as root without a password. Your prompt changes to mysql> when you are in.

Write mysql -u root -p. -u is the user. -p makes it ask for the password.

Write the same command with -h 192.168.1.10 (the host) and -P 3306 (the port) before -u root -p.

Prefer a window instead? Open the graphic tool and fill in these boxes:

BoxWhat to enter
Connection nameAnything, for example Local MySQL
Hostname127.0.0.1
Port3306

first_commands.sql

Once you are in, run these to prove the login works and see where you are.

Read the full code

Practise it part by part

Who am I?

Select VERSION(), then select CURRENT_USER().

List and leave
